Primary clinics doing the digital input. The plan of September 2022 lists focal points in health units and equipment for health centres to run DHIS2 among its actions, and states that health professionals were not adhering to the system even where it was available.

Not held. Which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, where the data is keyed and how many primary clinics enter their own reports are not established. No statement of who finances the system is held from the last three years, and the all-district implementation of 2024-2025 carries no month.

SWZ.short: Hospitals and maternities record births and deaths digitally (2022); DHIS2 introduced nationally in 2024; tiers reporting and clinics entering their own not established.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. WHO's country office places DHIS2 within the Ministry of Health's Strategic Health Information Department, run by its M&E unit, and reports that in 2024 it was hosted on UNICEF servers. MEASURE Evaluation's country profile of August 2019 records the Health Information System Strategic Plan 2010-2014 as not current.

Tiers in use. The Central Statistical Office's vital statistics report for 2022 shows an HMIS officer at the hospital or maternity recording birth and death outcomes in the Ministry of Health's inpatient system.

Where data is digitised. The same report shows the record made at the hospital or maternity itself, producing the ministry's hospital birth and death statistics, and HMIS supplied it with 28,541 health-institution births and 1,354 health-institution deaths for 2022.

Last twelve months. WHO's country office reports that DHIS2 was introduced nationally in 2024 as a single platform for health data that had sat in separate programme databases. The ministry's HMIS unit says that in the first quarter of 2026 reporting from CMIS, the national electronic medical record, to DHIS2 was strengthened with automated, FHIR-aligned data flows.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. MEASURE Evaluation's country profile of August 2019 records 95% of facilities as represented in HMIS information, and no electronic system for aggregating routine facility or community service data.

Not held. Nothing says which tiers send routine aggregate reports, where clinics' reports are keyed, or how many primary clinics enter their own. No plan or financing dated within the last three years is held.

SYC.short: The 2022 health plan calls data capture primarily paper-based with eHIS work stalled; no tier or clinic reporting digitally is held, setting no rung.
SYC.summary: Not held. No tier reporting digitally and no primary clinic entering its own reports is held. The ministry's 2022 plan describes data capture as primarily paper-based and its electronic system work as stalled, which is neither a dated statement of no digital entry at any level nor a contracted rollout.

TCD.short: Districts key health centres' monthly paper reports into DHIS2 (Gavi audit, 2024); no share or count of health centres entering their own reports is established.
TCD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Public Health and Prevention runs DHIS2 through its Direction des Statistiques et du Système d'Information Sanitaire, as the DHIS2 programme stated in November 2022. The ministry's PNDS 4 for 2022-2030, dated November 2022, sets the target of DHIS2 operational in all health districts by 2030. The World Bank's diagnostic states that DHIS2 was implemented in July 2021 with the financial support of the Global Fund and the GAVI Alliance.

Tiers in use. The Countdown to 2030 country team states that hospitals' migration from the old health information system to DHIS2 is very slow, with support to them running since 2022, as of 2023.

Where data is digitised. Gavi's programme audit, on site in August 2024, records that in one district the immunisation officer keys the monthly reports of 16 health centres into DHIS2 himself, and that entry for N'Djamena Centre district is likewise done at the district. The DHIS2 programme reports 96.4% of districts entering their data directly into DHIS2 after the national launch of November 2022. PNDS 4, of November 2022, lists extending DHIS2 to the health centres as an action still to be carried out.

Last twelve months. WHO's Chad office reports that during the 2024-2025 biennium its support contributed to the updating of the reporting tools and their integration into DHIS2.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Countdown to 2030 country team reports facility reporting rates above 90% since 2020, as of 2023.

Not held. No share or count of health centres entering their own reports is held. No financing dated within the last three years is held, and the digital health strategy adopted in 2024-2025 is not said to name the system.

TGO.short: 96.5% of all health facilities keyed complete reports into DHIS2 in 2021, per the ministry; no share for primary clinics alone, nothing newer.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's monitoring and evaluation plan for its national health development plan 2023-2027 of October 2023 names DHIS2 as the platform of what the ministry calls the SNIS, the national health information system, coordinated by its directorate DSNISI. The Global Fund's Office of the Inspector General reported in June 2025 that Global Fund investment in the health management information system and related systems is EUR 9.8 million in Grant Cycle 7, 2024 to 2026, and that Togo has no coordinated national digitalisation strategy for health.

Tiers in use. The plan names the peripheral care units (USP) and the CHP, CHR and CHU hospitals as the facilities producing and keying SNIS reports. The ministry's procedures manual of April 2022 states that DHIS2 was scaled up to all health facilities from 2018.

Where data is digitised. The plan requires each health facility to key its validated monthly or quarterly activity report into DHIS2 before the 5th of the following month.

Last twelve months. HISP's round-up for July 2026 reports a field mission to integrate the eRDQA data quality app into the national DHIS2 platform, tested at the regional hospitals of Sokodé and Dapaong and the health centres of Kadambara, Ataloté and Kpessidè.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry's plan gives 96.5% for 2021 as the share of all health facilities due to report that keyed a complete SNIS report into DHIS2. WHO Togo's 2024 annual report gives a completeness rate of 89.2% for 2021.

Not held. No share for primary clinics alone is held, nothing newer than 2021, and the 96.5% is printed without its counts. No domestic budget line is stated, and no count of community health workers keying their reports into DHIS2.

TUN.short: Nothing held on routine aggregate reporting at any tier; a unified national health information system named in 2021 with no use stated, so no rung.
TUN.summary: Not held. Nothing is held on routine aggregate reporting, at any tier. The ministry's performance report for 2021 names a unified national health information system being put in place and says nothing of its use.

TZA.short: Facilities report on paper and councils key into DHIS2 (2024); no share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's Monitoring and Evaluation Unit coordinated the HMIS data drawn from DHIS2 for 2024, with the University of Dar es Salaam and HISP Tanzania giving technical support in maintaining the platform. The Health Sector Strategic Plan V, for July 2021 to June 2026, carried strategic directions for strengthening the HMIS. Informants interviewed in April and May 2022 said most money for the HMIS was pooled from development partners in the Basket Fund and managed by government.

Tiers in use. The ministry's guidelines of May 2019 describe MTUHA, its name for the HMIS, as collecting routine data from dispensaries, health centres and council hospitals through the councils, while national, zonal, specialised and private hospitals use different platforms.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's methodology for its 2024 statistics states that each facility aggregates its registers and tally sheets monthly and the figures are entered into DHIS2 at council level, for 11,805 public and private health facilities.

Last twelve months. The University of Dar es Salaam's DHIS2 Lab reported on 1 October 2025 that a workshop led by the Ministry of Health Zanzibar validated data flows from programme and point-of-service systems into ZHMIS, Zanzibar's HMIS, and moved the integration towards the live environment.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The guidelines of May 2019 state that aggregated data is entered into DHIS in some health facilities, and at council level where facilities use paper.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held. No financing for the HMIS dated within the last three years is held, and no plan period after June 2026.

UGA.short: DHIS2 took reports from every tier in FY 2023/24; a Health Centre III carried its report to the district in 2026. No clinic share published.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's Division of Health Information manages DHIS2, which the ministry rolled out as the national reporting system to 112 districts in 2011, according to a study published in October 2025. The National Health Compact 2025-2030, adopted in December 2025, commits to scale DHIS2 up to all facilities, with 100% of hospitals and 80% of Health Centre IVs and IIIs reporting in real time by 2028.

Tiers in use. The ministry coded 6,546 health facilities in DHIS2 in FY 2023/24 and publishes DHIS2 figures by level, from national referral hospitals to Health Centre IIs and clinics. A census of all 265 government Health Centre IVs and hospitals, published in October 2025, found DHIS2 in use in 98.8% of them.

Where data is digitised. At a launch on 11 August 2026 the Uganda Muslim Medical Bureau said many Health Centre IIIs lack computers and connectivity to submit reports, and Ziiru Health Centre III carries its report to Buvuma district headquarters. In Health Centre IVs and hospitals, paper registers capture patient data, which is later aggregated and entered into DHIS2, on the October 2025 study's account.

Last twelve months. Makerere University's METS programme reported in April 2026 that reporting through DHIS2 rose from 58 percent in 2020 to 98 percent in 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry states that decentralising data entry to facilities continued in FY 2023/24.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and facility entry is established only for Health Centre IVs and hospitals. How DHIS2 is financed is not stated, and the 58 to 98 percent reporting rate has no stated measure or denominator.

ZAF.short: DHIS used at facility, district, province and national level, July 2026; no national share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Under the District Health Management Information System Policy, the Director-General has overall ownership of the District Health Information System and the Department of Health owns all its data, in the National Department of Health's bid terms of 24 July 2026. The department invites the bids itself, under National Treasury prescripts and priced in rand, for three years of hosting, maintenance, support and enhancement.

Tiers in use. The department described the system in July 2026 as used at facility, district, province and national level, reporting by clinic, community health centre and hospital.

Where data is digitised. Nine provincial instances capture the routine data and the national instance is filled by synchronisation, on the department's account of July 2026. The same bid plans training for 920 data capturers at primary health care clinics and 400 at district hospitals over three years.

Last twelve months. On 24 July 2026 the department issued bid NDOH 09/2025-2026 for a provider to host, maintain, support and enhance the system for three years, covering nine provincial DHIS2 instances, the national data warehouse and training of about 6,000 officials.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Thabethe and Mathews state that all public health facilities in Eastern Cape province used DHIS2, with capture by staff in the facility, over April 2017 to March 2020.

Not held. No national share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the one figure covers a single province. No health information plan dated within the last three years is held.

ZMB.short: DHIS2 is keyed monthly at district from paper, a few facilities entering directly (April 2024); no count or share of those facilities is held.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Gavi's programme audit of April 2024 calls DHIS2 the Ministry of Health's own system and "the approved country data management system". The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026, revised in February 2023 and costed at ZMW 158.3 billion, names the HMIS as a basis for monitoring the plan and sets out to integrate health information systems at different levels. For its 2023-2025 grant cycle the Global Fund finances the upgrade and maintenance of the DHIS2-based health management information system, as its case study of April 2025 states.

Tiers in use. Interviews of May and June 2019 found the HMIS collecting monthly reports from rural health posts, rural and urban health centres, and district and provincial hospitals.

Where data is digitised. Gavi's audit of April 2024 states that data entry into DHIS2 is done monthly at the district level, with a few health facilities reporting directly. The 2019 interviews describe facilities aggregating patient data onto paper reports each month and district information officers keying them into DHIS2.

Last twelve months. The Countdown to 2030 country team, from the University of Zambia and the Ministry of Health, states that 99% of expected monthly facility reports were in DHIS2 in 2024, against 93% in 2019.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Gavi's audit of April 2024 says that a few health facilities report directly into DHIS2, and cites 3,320 health facilities countrywide from a 2022 cold chain inventory.

Not held. No count or share of facilities entering their own reports is held; the 99% is a completeness rate and does not say where the data are keyed. The account of the tiers dates from 2019, and no dated event in the last twelve months is held.

ZWE.short: All four tiers report on paper, keyed into DHIS2 at the district (2023); no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is held.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The U.S. President's Malaria Initiative (PMI), in a profile published in 2023, describes DHIS2 as the Ministry of Health and Child Care's system, to which donors and partners have very limited access. The ministry's National Health Strategy 2021-2025 names DHIS2 among its routine aggregate systems for monitoring and evaluation. The Global Fund said in August 2025 that its financing supports data analysis and capacity building at sub-national levels of the national health management information system.

Tiers in use. PMI's 2023 profile states that the HMIS collects routine aggregate information from four levels: over 1,700 primary health centres, clinics and rural hospitals, about 140 district-level hospitals, eight provincial hospitals and six quaternary hospitals.

Where data is digitised. The same profile states that monthly collection is on paper at village, health facility and hospital levels, and that the district health information officer enters the paper records into the Zimbabwe DHIS2. A 2025 abstract on the DHIS2 community site states that facilities running Impilo, the ministry's patient record system, send data to DHIS2 by real-time, mobile-backup and manual-backup pipelines.

Last twelve months. The Countdown to 2030 synthesis report, written with ministry staff, states that the national reporting rate of health facility data in DHIS2 was above 92% in 2024.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. PMI's routine table gives 1,776 health facilities reporting into the HMIS/DHIS2 in 2022, with 96% of expected monthly reports received.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 96% counts reports received. No strategy current at 30 September 2026 is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

AGO.short: One hospital's obstetric record prototype under test, keyed retrospectively (2019); nothing since, so tiers, clinic use and governance not established.
AGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The electronic obstetric record prototype at the Irene Neto Maternity Hospital in Lubango was part of a doctoral research project at the University of Beira Interior, Portugal, adapting ObsCare, an application owned by Virtual Care, as its authors stated in November 2019.

Tiers in use. The prototype ran at one 180-bed maternity hospital in November 2019.

Where data is digitised. At that hospital the clinical processes of deliveries from the fourth quarter of 2016 were being entered retrospectively in the admission, archive and medical statistics section in November 2019. Luanda's two reference tuberculosis facilities kept clinical and surveillance data entirely on paper records and registers between March and September 2019.

Last twelve months. The prototype was in its test phase in November 2019.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Anti-Tuberculosis Dispensary of Luanda recorded on paper medical records and registers in 2019.

Not held. Nothing is dated after 2019, so whether the prototype still runs is not established. No source names the tiers holding an EMR, any primary clinic using one, or who governs one.

BDI.short: 41 of 71 hospitals held a patient record and six health centres piloted one (2023); no shared record or later coverage is established.
BDI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. OpenClinic sits under Enabel and PROGISSA, the health informatics programme the ministry created in 2020, the World Bank reported in March 2023. In a memorandum signed on 6 February 2026 the government commits to use SIDAinfo as its electronic medical records system, and the United States intends to fund it with $565,579 in 2026.

Tiers in use. Forty-one of 71 public and faith-based hospitals are computerised, patient health records included, and 39 of them run OpenClinic, the World Bank reported in March 2023, citing PROGISSA. They are not interconnected and each has its own patient identifier.

Where data is digitised. In the computerised hospitals OpenClinic GA runs on a local server in each hospital, with data passing between clinical services, laboratory, imaging and pharmacy in real time without further manual entry, the ministry's plan drawn up in 2019 states.

Last twelve months. The memorandum of 6 February 2026 commits Burundi to roll SIDAinfo out in 460 facilities by 2026 and 572 by 2028.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Six health centres are computerised under a pilot financed by Enabel, the World Bank reported in March 2023, with 29 more on Enabel's financing and four on the government's planned during that year. The ministry's 2019 plan puts first-level facilities at more than 1,000.

Not held. No count of health centres on a patient record is dated since March 2023, and the 460 facilities of the 2026 memorandum are a commitment with no tier given. The 41 hospitals are not broken down by tier, and whether SIDAinfo, recorded in 2023 as a record of people living with HIV, serves general care is not established.

BEN.short: Only a pledged digital health booklet is held, from 2026; no source states a tier, where records are digitised, or that they are on paper.
BEN.summary: Not held. No source held states a tier, a place of digitisation or a clinic count for an electronic medical record, or that patient records are on paper at every tier. A digital health booklet is held only as a pledge.

BFA.short: OpenClinic ran at two pilot hospitals in 2025 and one package at a university hospital (2023); primary clinics and point-of-care recording are not established.
BFA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. NetAfrique reported on 18 July 2025 that the Ministry of Health, through its Direction des systèmes d'information, trains the administrators of OpenClinic, a tool chosen at a workshop with the directors general of all university and regional hospitals. A paper on the 2024-2025 pilot describes OpenClinic GA as a nationally governed open-source hospital information system, customised under a national reference framework. ICTworks lists the Plan stratégique de la santé numérique 2025-2029, signed in January 2025, as the operative strategy.

Tiers in use. OpenClinic, a hospital management system with clinical and nursing records, is deployed at pilot sites, the CHUR of Ouahigouya and the CHR of Manga, NetAfrique reported on 18 July 2025. At Manga the 2024-2025 pilot ended in full digitisation of admissions and use of the electronic patient record across multiple departments. A study with fieldwork from September 2022 to April 2023 found one patient-record package fully deployed in a public university hospital.

Where data is digitised. A study with fieldwork from September 2022 to April 2023 found that the predominant data collection instruments in health facilities were physical consultation registers.

Last twelve months. NetAfrique reported on 18 July 2025 the ministry's second training session for OpenClinic administrators, in the Nazinon region.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. By April 2023 the public health system lacked computerised patient records, those in existence being electronic registers or isolated specialty records in a hospital, a study of 35 digital health interventions found.

Not held. The position at primary clinics is not established, nor whether the pilot hospitals record at the point of care or key afterwards. Nothing held is dated within the last twelve months, and who finances the systems is not held.

BWA.short: All public hospitals held an electronic record (2019-20) and a centralised EMR reached 22 facilities in one district (March 2026); no shared record is established.
BWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's budget speech of 5 March 2026 states that it and the Ministry of Local Government and Traditional Affairs will roll out the completed EMR to the remaining 29 districts in 2026/27. The 2026/27 development budget request allocates P62,534,000 to the ministry's headquarters, naming the Digitalization of Health Services Project. A World Bank technical note published on 30 October 2025 costs the electronic medical record at US$1.531 million, from an IBRD loan.

Tiers in use. MEASURE Evaluation's profile of August 2019 states that all hospitals are on a centralised Integrated Patient Management System, the ministry's name for it. A 2019-20 survey names 13 public hospitals using it, from referral to primary hospitals.

Where data is digitised. The National eHealth Strategy adopted in March 2020 is quoted as saying the public hospitals' electronic medical record is real time. A survey of 2019-20 found most eRecord systems not interoperable within or between facilities, and no national unique patient identifier.

Last twelve months. On 19 November 2025 the Minister of Local Government told Parliament that the Electronic Medical Records system was being piloted in two districts. The March 2026 budget speech reports 21 more facilities in Okavango due by the end of that month.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Assistant Minister of Health told Parliament on 5 March 2026 that Phase 1 of the ministry's centralised Electronic Medical Record had been implemented in 22 health facilities in Ngami.

Not held. No unique patient identifier in use, and no retrieval of a record at another facility, is established. The types of the 22 facilities and a national denominator are not given, hospital coverage after 2020 is not held, and no plan dated within the last three years is held.

CAF.short: e-SENI in phased deployment at hospitals and health centres (2026); number of sites, hospital level and any clinics figure not established.
CAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. HISP Rwanda is supporting deployment of the HISP EMR, known in the country as e-SENI, in partnership with the Ministry of Health and the Susan Buffett Foundation under the SENI project, as it reported on 18 March 2026.

Tiers in use. HISP Rwanda's team supervised implementation of e-SENI at hospital and health centres, on its account of March 2026.

Where data is digitised. e-SENI gives each patient a unique identification and a centralised record captured in real time across clinical units, from registration and consultation to laboratory and pharmacy. The record is shared within the facility and synchronised to a central EMR server, as HISP Rwanda described it in March 2026.

Last twelve months. HISP Rwanda reported on 18 March 2026 a phased deployment under way, with site assessments, configuration in French, staff training, an EMR showroom and a central synchronisation server set up.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. HISP Rwanda states that medical records in many facilities are still kept in paper registers, as of March 2026.

Not held. The number of e-SENI sites, the hospitals' level, any district coverage and any clinics figure are not held, nor the system's owner or a plan. The deployment is undated, and the record is not said to be retrievable at another facility.

CIV.short: The ministry's patient record ran in every service of one general hospital from August 2024; the 268 establishments connected by March 2025 carry no tier.
CIV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's digital health directorate presents the Dossier Patient Informatisé (DPI) as a platform of the ministry, deployed in August 2024 by a team the directorate led. On 25 March 2025 the project's steering committee set itself to define a detailed plan for digitalising the health system. The World Bank's appraisal of 18 September 2025 states that Phase 1 of RAPID-CI, an IDA credit of EUR 128.6 million, will support the rollout of an electronic patient records system across several levels of care.

Tiers in use. The DPI has been operational at the Hôpital Général de Ferkessédougou since 16 August 2024, used by all the hospital's services, the directorate reports.

Where data is digitised. At Ferkessédougou the platform is installed on the hospital's local server and every service registers and follows patients on it, from 16 August 2024.

Last twelve months. On 22 April 2026 the health ministry noted the deployment of the DPI as an advance under way and prioritised 150 first-contact establishments for connectivity in 2026. A national workshop closing on 4 September 2026 retained the computerised patient record among ten quick wins to be put into service before the end of 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The project unit told the steering committee on 25 March 2025 that the first phase had connected 268 health establishments to the hospital information system and the DPI. The health minister counted both installed in 193 health establishments in 2023.

Not held. The tiers of the 268 establishments and the total they are drawn from are not stated, and use of the record is shown at one general hospital only. Whether a patient's record can be retrieved at another facility is not established, and no primary clinic is shown using it.

CMR.short: Ministry's Bahmni record deployed in about fifty pilot facilities (2020-2024); their level, routine hospital use and a procured national record are not established.
CMR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Public Health's digital health plan for 2026 to 2030 budgets for 2026 the selection of a partner and a public-private partnership contract to deploy an electronic medical record, and names the record among projects that drew on partner financing under the 2020-2024 plan. SmartMobileClinic, launched in 2022, is run by the German association Mapubi e.V. with the Health and Research Organisation Cameroon.

Tiers in use. At Yaoundé Central Hospital, a national referral hospital, a clinical information system built on MediBoard was deployed in the gynaecology-obstetrics department and counted 113 users and 1,278 patient records after six months, on its authors' account published in October 2023. Staff stopped entering data when the per-entry payment ended.

Where data is digitised. In that department data were entered on computers in consultation and treatment rooms, with paper service registers kept in parallel. EcoMatin reported in September 2023 that in almost all public hospitals patient files are kept on paper.

Last twelve months. From September 2025 SmartMobileClinic was extended to further rural communities, with 12 rural campaigns between November 2025 and January 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry states that its electronic medical record, which it calls the DME and runs on Bahmni, was deployed in about fifty pilot health facilities during the 2020-2024 plan. The SmartMobileClinic project runs campaigns with local health facilities in 12 rural communities.

Not held. The level of the fifty or so pilot facilities is not stated, and no count of facilities using SmartMobileClinic is given. Routine use at any hospital is not established, and no national record has been procured.

COD.short: Equipment for approved hospital information systems delivered (2024–25) and approval opened (2026); no facility is stated to be using a patient record.
COD.summary: Not held. No source held states that any facility uses an electronic patient record: the hospital information systems ANICNS approves are described as delivered or to come, and Visa Medical's deployment names no site. The one survey held, of seven hospitals in Kananga in 2023, does not carry the country.

COG.short: A public hospital's organisation decree (gazetted February 2026) names a hospital information system, not said to hold clinical records; no source describes patient records.
COG.summary: Not held. No statement of whether patient records are kept on paper or digitally, at any tier, is held. A public hospital's organisation decree names a hospital information system without saying that it holds the clinical record.

COM.short: The Ministry stated in July 2021 that no electronic patient record exists in the country; nothing dated since confirms or replaces it.
COM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's digital health strategy for 2022 to 2026, dated July 2021, lists the electronic patient record, which it calls the Dossier Electronique du Patient, among the components absent from the country. It plans a modular application for reception, consultations, tests, hospitalisation and billing, in more than 40 structures by the end of 2024.

Tiers in use. In July 2021 the ministry stated that the electronic patient record does not exist in the country.

Where data is digitised. The same strategy lists telemedicine, m-health applications and online training as absent alongside the patient record.

Last twelve months. The World Bank recorded a hospital management information system as not functional at 31 August 2024, against a target of functional by December 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In July 2021 only CHN El Maarouf, CHRI Hombo and the medical imaging centre had internet, and district health centres were rarely connected.

Not held. Nothing dated after July 2021 confirms or replaces the ministry's statement, which does not say in words that records are on paper. The hospital management information system is not said to hold the clinical record.

CPV.short: Medicine One in use only in Praia's health centres and central hospital, February 2024; no site count, place of entry or clinic share established.
CPV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's terms of reference published in February 2024 name Medicine One as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry, a proprietary product licensed per workstation and per period. They state that the government's digital governance strategy takes health as a priority and includes a single-platform health project, under which the ministry plans what it calls a single electronic clinical process for all health structures, public and private.

Tiers in use. As at February 2024 Medicine One was in use only in Praia's health facilities, namely its health centres and the central hospital. The ministry gives the software's complexity, per-workstation licence costs and bandwidth needs as the reasons.

Where data is digitised. Medicine One was brought in with the Electronic Prescription Project to centralise clinical history in a single electronic repository, on the ministry's account of February 2024.

Last twelve months. On 18 December 2025 the Minister of Health, Jorge Figueiredo, announced that each citizen will get a unique patient code giving access to a digital clinical history, with digital medical records centralising clinical data across facilities.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Praia's health centres were the only ones using Medicine One in May 2023, and the position was the same in February 2024.

Not held. No count of sites, place of entry or share of primary clinics is held, and nothing after February 2024 says what is in use. The patient code and digital clinical history announced in December 2025 are not shown in use.

DJI.short: A 2024 report describes paper medical follow-up, naming no tier or system; no EMR is named at any tier, so no rung is set.
DJI.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record is named at any tier, and no statement that patient records are on paper at every tier is held. The one statement held, of 2024, describes medical follow-up on paper and names no tier and no system.

DZA.short: An electronic medical record is placed in hospitals in September 2026; no count of hospitals and nothing on primary clinics is established.
DZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health updated the patient's electronic record itself, drawing on nearly 700 proposals from the sector, and its minister presented the new version on 26 February 2024. In Annaba the ministry's services coordinate preparation of what Seybouse Times calls the Dossier médical électronique with the wilaya health directorate and Algérie Télécom, as of 16 August 2026.

Tiers in use. An El Moudjahid editorial of 8 September 2026 places the electronic medical record system in the country's hospital establishments. From 2018 the ministry put an earlier record, DEMDZ, into certain pilot hospitals, the Tizi-Ouzou university hospital among them. At that hospital, Salmi, Bouchelaghem and Mohellebi wrote in 2022, the use of DEMDZ failed and only the laboratory and radiology parts of a computerised patient record were in use.

Where data is digitised. The version presented to hospital directors on 26 February 2024 carries a national identification number for each patient and holds all the patient's personal and medical data. The minister said any hospital establishment in the country can access it.

Last twelve months. On 16 August 2026 the Annaba health directorate, the Ministry of Health and Algérie Télécom met to speed up the fibre-optic connection of health structures, in preparation for the record's implementation in the wilaya, Seybouse Times reported.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Seybouse Times describes the record's progressive roll-out in the health structures of the wilaya of Annaba as still forthcoming in mid-August 2026.

Not held. No count or share of hospitals using the record is held, and nothing on primary clinics. Where the record is keyed, a plan naming it and its financing are not stated.

EGY.short: Electronic health records are at early pilots (government compact, December 2025); no count of hospitals or clinics with a denominator is established.
EGY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Egypt Healthcare Authority runs a unified electronic medical record, as it said on 19 August 2024. The National Health Strategy 2024-2030 names a unified electronic medical record among its key actions, with hospitals of all providers and all primary care units to be automated to support it. The health ministry disclosed neither the cost nor the financing of the platform it proposed in September 2026.

Tiers in use. The Authority said on 19 August 2024 that, in the governorates where Universal Health Insurance applies, its hospitals work on a fully computerised system, its primary healthcare centres and units are fully digitised, and referral from them to higher levels is electronic. CIPIT's report of June 2025 states that Egypt has deployed electronic health record systems in public hospitals.

Where data is digitised. A Cairo University study of Omrania family health centre in Giza, observed from September 2016 to December 2019, found patient records kept as paper family files, fetched by a clerk and handed to the physician.

Last twelve months. The health minister discussed a proposed "Egypt Smart Healthcare Platform" with MTS and Inspur, to hold unified patient records shared between facilities, and a pilot for its first phase, as reported on 14 September 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The government's National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 describes electronic health records in Egypt as at the stage of early pilots.

Not held. No count of hospitals or clinics with a denominator is held, nor the number of governorates the Authority's record covers, and its 2024 statement is not reconciled with the compact's early pilots of 2025. No dated fact after 2019 shows where the record is entered, and the September 2026 proposal carries no timetable.

ERI.short: Only a DHIS2 tracker programme and unspecified patient-level systems held; no EMR named, no dated statement of paper records, so no rung.
ERI.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record is named at any tier. No dated statement that patient records are on paper at every tier is held.

ETH.short: Over 70 facilities had an EMR by December 2024, 10 paperless; national pilot due 2026. Tier, denominator and use across most hospitals not established.
ETH.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health presents electronic medical records as a milestone of its own digital health work in December 2024. The memorandum signed with the United States on 23 December 2025 schedules a national multi-tenant EMR: piloting in 2026, 48 facilities by 2027 and 438 by 2030. The United States plans to support its customisation and roll-out, Ethiopia paying the licensing, cloud and hardware costs the United States does not.

Tiers in use. EMR systems are implemented in health centres and hospitals, as the Central Ethiopia Regional Health Bureau states. In June 2023 the Bahmni EMR was in use at one general hospital and three health centres in Addis Ababa.

Where data is digitised. Providers at those four facilities entered consultations, prescriptions and laboratory orders in the EMR during care in June 2023, and the record was used across the departments of the one facility. The Ministry of Health states that 10 of the facilities with an EMR operate entirely paperless in December 2024.

Last twelve months. On 23 December 2025 Ethiopia and the United States signed the memorandum, with activities from 1 April 2026 to 31 December 2030.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Ministry of Health states that electronic medical records were introduced in over 70 health facilities in the three years to December 2024. The memorandum of 23 December 2025 gives a baseline of 0% of hospitals and health centres implementing the full national EMR.

Not held. The tier of the 70-plus facilities and the total they are drawn from are not held, and the 0% counts the full national system only. Neither most referral and district hospitals nor primary clinics across any district are shown using an EMR; the named primary sites are three health centres in Addis Ababa.

GAB.short: eGabon-SIS ran in 13 pilot sites in Grand Libreville in February 2026, two of them health centres; no primary-clinic count or denominator established.
GAB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The state digital agency ANINF implements the health information system Gabon calls eGabon-SIS, with a project technical committee following it, as Gabonactu reported on 25 October 2025. Its supplier won a tender launched by the Ministry of Health, the contract handed over on 16 February 2024. The World Bank approved a US$56 million loan on 3 June 2016, US$40.08 million of it for the national health information system. The project was officially closed on 24 June 2026.

Tiers in use. On 11 February 2026 the system worked in 13 pilot sites across Grand Libreville, the Egypt-Gabon cooperation hospital among them, with the Libreville university hospital and the regional hospitals not yet covered, on Gabonactu's account.

Where data is digitised. On 23 October 2025 the chief doctor of the Lalala health centre in Libreville said a patient can now be found in different facilities under a unique identifier.

Last twelve months. On 11 February 2026 the health minister asked the World Bank, which agreed, to bring the system into the Libreville university hospital. At the project's closing on 24 June 2026 the authorities named maintenance, cybersecurity, training and extension to the whole territory as the next priorities.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Two health centres, Lalala and Glass, were confirmed using the system on 23 October 2025, among 13 pilot sites in Grand Libreville.

Not held. No count of primary clinics using the system and no denominator is held, and use at a national or referral hospital is not established. Whether records are entered at the point of care is not stated, and no plan naming the system or domestic budget line is held.

GHA.short: LHIMS's contract lapsed in December 2024; GHIMS was ordered in October 2025; 15% of all health facilities have EMRs (2025 plan); GHIMS's reach not established.
GHA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. By a directive of 28 October 2025 the Ministry of Health named its Chief Director to lead the national rollout of the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS), with Axon Information Systems implementing it under government oversight. The ministry's Health Sector Medium-Term Development Plan 2026-2029, of October 2025, carries a national indicator for the percentage of health facilities with functional EMR systems in use.

Tiers in use. The Vice President said on 31 October 2024 that the Lightwave system LHIMS was deployed in all six teaching hospitals, 10 regional hospitals and 243 district hospitals. Its vendor's contract expired on 31 December 2024.

Where data is digitised. OneHealthEHR Inc. said in September 2026 that on its platform, in use in Liberia and Ghana, clinicians record patient information during care and synchronise it when a connection returns.

Last twelve months. The directive of 28 October 2025 ordered GHIMS rolled out nationwide in November 2025 as the only authorised platform for patient registration and clinical documentation, and cited nationwide disruptions to the existing clinical information and billing systems. OneHealthEHR says its platform went into live clinical use in Liberia and Ghana on 1 September 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry's plan of October 2025 gives 15% as the first value against its indicator for the percentage of all health facilities with functional EMR systems in use. OneHealthEHR reported seven active clinics and health centres across Liberia and Ghana together by late September 2026.

Not held. Which tiers and how many facilities use GHIMS is not established, nor whether LHIMS was shut down outright or disrupted in some hospitals. The 15% has no numerator, denominator or baseline year, GHIMS's financing is not stated, and the OneHealthEHR figures give no count for Ghana.

GIN.short: Three separate records ran in some hospitals and pilot facilities in 2026, entered at point of care; no hospital denominator or health-centre count held.
GIN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Visa Medical, a digital medical record, is built and run by the private start-up Kouma Academy with the Ministry of Health's support, as reported in August 2026. The OpenClinic hospital information system was installed in five facilities with the support of the Belgian agency Enabel. The non-profit Clinic+O runs its record in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, and the Swiss Re Foundation funds the project from November 2025 to December 2026.

Tiers in use. By August 2026 Visa Medical was deployed in 19 public establishments, Dubréka hospital among them. A ministry mission of 17 to 22 August 2026 reviewed five digitised facilities in the Mamou and Dalaba districts running OpenClinic, the Dalaba prefectural hospital among them. The Swiss Re Foundation's page of March 2026 has the Clinic+O record in use in rural communities and at Community Health Centers.

Where data is digitised. At Dubréka hospital in August 2026 clinicians retrieved a patient's consultations and tests in real time from the Visa Medical record. In the five Mamou and Dalaba facilities data are entered directly into OpenClinic. Clinic+O's community health workers capture patient information on tablets in an offline-first electronic medical record.

Last twelve months. The Dalaba prefectural hospital deployed OpenClinic in January 2026. The Clinic+O project began in November 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Swiss Re Foundation stated in March 2026 that Guinea's rural Community Health Centers are often understaffed and rely on paper-based systems.

Not held. No count of hospitals is held against which the 19 Visa Medical establishments and the five OpenClinic facilities can be set, and no count or district for the health centres using Clinic+O. Whether a Visa Medical record can be retrieved at another facility is not stated, and no plan naming any of the three systems is held.

GMB.short: One referral hospital piloted an electronic medical record in 2023; whether it or a contracted four-facility pilot still runs is not established.
GMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030, published in February 2024, states the need to establish an Electronic Medical Record System across all levels and for the Ministry of Health to integrate existing databases into one system. In June 2023 the World Bank stated that the Bluesquare contract for the electronic National Health Insurance System, under the Bank's Essential Health Services Strengthening Project, was amended to include an electronic health records system using OpenClinic.

Tiers in use. The Point reported in August 2023 the pilot launch of an Electronic Medical Records system at Edward Francis Small Teaching Hospital, the country's main referral hospital, developed by the Medical Research Council Unit The Gambia. The policy of February 2024 states that the health sector does not have a robust electronic medical record system in place.

Where data is digitised. The policy sets the strategy of migrating fully from paper-based recording to a computerised system at all levels of care.

Last twelve months. The World Bank's identity diagnostic of 2025 describes what it calls the Health Management Information System as managing patient records and issuing health cards, with the national identification number of the civil registration system identifying each patient.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In June 2023 the World Bank described the OpenClinic system as still to be piloted, in four health facilities.

Not held. Whether the teaching hospital's pilot of 2023 or the contracted pilot in four facilities was running at 30 September 2026 is not established, and no primary clinic figure is held. No facility is named for the patient record system described in 2025.

GNB.short: One private Bissau clinic's electronic patient record is held, as at June 2023; no source gives tiers or primary clinics, so no rung is set.
GNB.summary: Not held. The one electronic patient record held is at a single private clinic in Bissau, as at June 2023, and its tier is not stated. Nothing is held on tiers, primary clinics, governance or the last twelve months, and no admissible source states that patient records are on paper.

GNQ.short: Only DHIS2 trackers for vaccination and HIV follow-up are held, of 2025; no patient record system or paper position is stated, so no rung.
GNQ.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record is named at any tier, and no statement that patient records are on paper at every tier is held. On the patient side only programme trackers for routine vaccination and HIV follow-up are held.

KEN.short: Public Level 2 to 4 facilities reported migrated to the government's HMIS (September 2026); a shared record and primary clinics' own entry are not established.
KEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The US-Kenya Cooperation Framework signed on 4 December 2025 describes TaifaCare HMIS, a hospital management system with clinical modules, as the Government of Kenya's flagship system for health facilities, deployed and maintained by the government. It sets deployment at 2,000 public and faith-based facilities by 2026, 4,000 by 2027 and 8,000 by 2028. The United States intends to provide US$175 million for data systems, and Kenya intends to pay the ongoing licensing, cloud and hardware costs the United States does not.

Tiers in use. By 30 September 2026 all public Level 2 to 4 facilities were reported migrated from the Social Health Authority's provider portal to HMIS, the government's name for the facility system.

Where data is digitised. At the private network Penda Health, clinical officers recorded consultations directly in a cloud-based EMR at the point of care between April and July 2025. Regulations in force from 11 April 2025 require certified systems to query and update a shared health record within twenty-four hours of each encounter.

Last twelve months. The government set 30 September 2026 for facilities to move to HMIS, then extended the deadline to 30 October 2026, with 28 private platforms certified by the Digital Health Agency.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Framework states that TaifaCare HMIS was deployed in 1,500 public health facilities by 4 December 2025. Penda Health ran the same EMR in its 16 primary care clinics in Nairobi and Kiambu counties in 2025.

Not held. Nothing held shows a patient's record retrieved at another facility in practice, or what share of primary clinics have clinicians entering patient records. Use across the national referral hospitals is not established, and no budget line for the system is named.

LBR.short: A vendor's platform runs at a handful of pilot clinics and health centers (September 2026); the number of Liberian facilities live is not established.
LBR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. OneHealthEHR Inc. deploys and runs its platform with a consortium of European firms and research bodies, with the National Public Health Institute of Liberia as surveillance partner, as reported in September 2026. In the memorandum signed with the United States on 9 December 2025, Liberia commits to an open-source EMR in clinics, health centers and hospitals, with targets of 20% of all public health facilities in 2026 and 100% in 2030, and the United States plans US$2,676,744 for EMR systems over 2026 to 2030.

Tiers in use. The OneHealthEHR platform is in use at clinics and health centers, as reported in September 2026.

Where data is digitised. The company said in September 2026 that clinicians, nurses and registration staff record patient information in the platform during routine care, offline, with synchronisation when a connection returns.

Last twelve months. The company says its platform went into live clinical use on 1 September 2026 at four facilities across Liberia and Ghana. The Ministry of Health, through its National Health Intelligence Center, launched enumerator training on 8 May 2026 for a nationwide EMR readiness assessment. UNFPA issued a request for quotation dated 27 October 2025 for an EMR at Careysburg and Duport Road Health Centers.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. By the company's account, the deployment grew from four to seven active clinics and health centers, counted across Liberia and Ghana together, within about three weeks of 1 September 2026.

Not held. The number of Liberian facilities live is not held: the count of seven covers Liberia and Ghana together. Whether the OpenMRS system launched at J.J. Dossen Hospital in 2020 still runs is not on record.

LBY.short: One teaching hospital partly applying a system, reported in 2025, and a two-clinic trial in 2022; nothing shows the trial continuing.
LBY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Libya Herald described the Unified Electronic Health File System in May 2022 as a Ministry of Health project under implementation for more than five years. The National Centre for Health System Reform, under the ministry's supervision, launched the National Comprehensive Health Care Programme and the Health Number System in Tripoli in January 2024, as the ministry's strategic option for implementing the electronic health file. WHO states that in 2024 the ministry and WHO developed a digital transformation roadmap for 2025-2030 that promotes electronic health records and hospital management systems on open-source platforms.

Tiers in use. A Sabratha University field study published in December 2025 says that Sabratha Teaching Hospital has moved to apply an electronic medical records system and that difficulties prevent its full use.

Where data is digitised. At the May 2022 trial of the Unified Electronic Health File System, its technical committee showed information being entered directly from patients attending the clinic. The Sabratha study's author states that most public hospitals in Libya use traditional paper records.

Last twelve months. The Sabratha study, published on 24 December 2025, states that the move towards electronic medical records is slow or stalled in many government hospitals.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Libya Herald reports that the trial operation of the system was inaugurated in May 2022, with the first phase covering two sites, the Ghout al-Shaal clinic in Tripoli and the al-Kish clinic in Benghazi.

Not held. Nothing held shows the 2022 two-clinic trial continuing, or the electronic health file launched in January 2024 in use anywhere. No finance source is stated, and no dated event in the last twelve months is held.

LSO.short: eRegister in 197 public facilities (November 2025); general care recorded on paper at rural health centres (2023); no denominator or hospital-clinic split held.
LSO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's HIV programme stated in November 2025 that the plan is for the Government of Lesotho to completely own the EMR, using domestic resources. After the US stop-work orders of 2025 the government hired 10 IT and 10 HMIS personnel to support districts. The MCC compact of 12 May 2022 funds the expansion of the e-Register, which it says is limited to HIV and tuberculosis patients, into a national electronic medical record system covering all primary health care patients.

Tiers in use. A hospital-based EMR was introduced in 2013 across 16 public hospitals in the 10 districts. The ministry's assessment of 18 October 2017 found it discontinued in several facilities and in substandard use in others, and the HMIS Strategic Plan 2018-2022 records it at six hospitals, where clinicians and pharmacists used it inadequately.

Where data is digitised. MCC wrote on 11 December 2023 that at a rural health centre a pregnant woman who tests negative for HIV or TB has her care recorded on paper, in a health booklet, while an HIV-positive patient's care is recorded in an electronic medical record.

Last twelve months. The HIV programme states that the EMRs stayed in place through the 2025 US funding cuts, and that suboptimal use of the eRegister led to under-reporting of new ART initiations to September 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The HIV programme stated in November 2025 that what it calls the OpenMRS/Bahmni-based EMR/eRegister is in 197 public facilities.

Not held. No denominator for the 197 facilities is held, nor a split of hospitals from clinics, and nothing shows the expansion to all primary care patients delivered. The hospital EMR's standing after 2018 is not established, and no plan naming the system is held.

MAR.short: Hospital system stated as deployed in all public hospitals (2024), with keyed patient files in one province's primary clinics; no shared record, no clinic count.
MAR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Framework law 06-22 of 9 December 2022 creates a shared medical record within the national health information system. Nichan reported on 23 July 2024 that the health ministry was preparing to buy a national system built on a shared patient file, at an estimated 189,999,000 dirham.

Tiers in use. A government document published in December 2024 states that the integrated hospital information system has been deployed in all public hospitals of the twelve regions. A purchase notice of 23 April 2024 places the HOSIX patient-file database in the primary health care establishments of Taounate province.

Where data is digitised. At the CHU Mohammed VI in Marrakech, doctors write observations and diagnoses in HOSIX and order laboratory tests there, with the paper record kept alongside, a thesis defended on 29 May 2024 reports. The Taounate notice buys 19,200 working hours of contracted staff to key patient files into HOSIX.

Last twelve months. Medias24 reported in July 2026 that the Government Council had adopted draft law 52.26, which creates a shared medical record for every patient. The health minister said on 1 June 2026 that the ministry is still working to put the unified medical record in place.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The same document has an information system for primary health care establishments in the course of deployment. The ministry said on 5 April 2026 that work continues with the generalisation of the electronic medical record.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics using a patient record is held, and no count of hospitals using the hospital system; primary-tier use is held for one province. No shared record is in service, and the financing of the planned national system is not stated.

MDG.short: Electronic records run in some private establishments and some health centres (2024); no count, share or district is held, and no hospital use.
MDG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's PSRSIS 2023-2027 lists as an activity the development of a patient management and electronic reporting system for all care structures. The computerised patient record software used in community medical centres is Datasanté's, under a partnership with the community doctors' association AMC-MAD renewed by a convention signed on 6 November 2024, which provides for Datasanté's continued logistical and financial support.

Tiers in use. At a round table on 5 November 2024 attended by the health ministry, the electronic personal medical record was described as functional in some private establishments and some basic health centres.

Where data is digitised. A community doctor at Matielona, equipped by Datasanté in November 2019, states that she keeps no paper register and that everything is in each patient's computerised record, entered on a tablet. A 2021 assessment of 30 health centres in two regions names paper registers as their primary documents for recording patient information.

Last twelve months. In January 2025, 2424.mg reported that two pilot sites had been chosen to start the hospital digitalisation project, the CHU Ravoahangy Andrianavalona and the CHUSSPA at Analakely, a project initiated by the digital development ministry with the Ministry of Public Health.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry's digital health strategy of January 2023 states that management of clinical data and of the hospital information system remains at an experimental and local stage, and that patient-management applications are used in private practices and private health centres.

Not held. No count, share or district is held for the facilities keeping an electronic record, and no hospital is shown using one. Nothing held is dated within the last twelve months.

MLI.short: One Bamako hospital with a point-of-care circuit (2026), 27 project-equipped CSCom (2022); use by most hospitals or by clinics across districts is not established.
MLI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's agency ANTIM introduced and runs the OpenClinic GA deployments in community health centres, reference health centres and hospitals, it told USAID in July 2022; those in community health centres were launched with support from Global Affairs Canada. The ministry's digital health plan for 2024 to 2028 sets 75% of health establishments using a harmonised, computerised or shared medical record by 2028.

Tiers in use. On 27 July 2026 the Hôpital dermatologie de Bamako ran a fully digitised consultation circuit, from registration through consultation and laboratory to pharmacy, the ministry's communication network reports. In July 2022 ANTIM had digitalized a dozen of the 65 reference health centers and was working to digitalize 5 of the 13 hospitals.

Where data is digitised. At that hospital on 27 July 2026 registration, consultation, laboratory and pharmacy each worked in the system on the patient's unique number as the patient passed through.

Last twelve months. OpenClinic was presented to the Prime Minister on 16 September 2025 as the health ministry's tool centralising patient records, Ecofin Agency reports.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The SanDi project of 2021 to 2022 deployed OpenClinic in 27 community health centres, a University of Sherbrooke poster of 2024 says. Pilots to digitise patient files in a few community health centres did not succeed, for lack of funding and institutional support, the World Bank's diagnostic of 2023 states.

Not held. Nothing held shows most national, regional or district hospitals, or primary clinics across named districts, keeping the record, and the 27 centres carry no denominator or statement of routine use. No financing within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

MOZ.short: One hospital, Mavalane General, went digital with SIS-H in December 2024; point-of-care use, SIS-RME's release and any clinic count are not established.
MOZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health memorandum signed with the United States on 15 December 2025 states that the Integrated Electronic Medical Record System (SIS-RME), as it names it, is owned and operated by the Government of Mozambique, and names it the core product of the national digital health platform. The United States plans to fund SIS-RME's software development and equipment within US$83,072,079 of data-systems funding over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. Jembi Health Systems states that in December 2024 Mavalane General Hospital in Maputo became Mozambique's first digital hospital, its Hospital Health Information System (SIS-H) digitising admissions and inpatient care and replacing paper records.

Where data is digitised. At the eight health units visited in a 2019 assessment with the ministry, daily registries were kept in paper books and charts, beside tablets supplied by particular programmes. In 2016-17 patient data at 16 public primary care facilities were recorded daily in paper registers and tally sheets.

Last twelve months. The memorandum of 15 December 2025 targets a minimum viable version of SIS-RME for September 2026 and a scannable data-capture solution for low-burden health facilities by the end of June 2027. The ministry states that it singles out implementation of the Electronic Medical Record starting from the health units.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. None of the 16 public primary care facilities selected for the 2016-17 study had an electronic system.

Not held. Nothing held shows whether the record at Mavalane is kept at the point of care or shared, or who owns SIS-H. No release of SIS-RME or facility using it is held, the paper position at primary facilities dates from 2017 and 2019, and no count or share of clinics is held.

MRT.short: One pilot health centre, Sebkha, had digitised patient records (2022); nothing later shows whether it still runs or has spread.
MRT.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The European Commission's 2025 action document for PASS IV states that Mauritania's digital health strategy 2024-2030 is to be deployed through telemedicine, electronic medical records and integrated management systems, and sets aside EUR 3,000,000 for procurement under the output that names the patient record. The National Digital Transformation Agenda of June 2022 names the Ministry of Health as carrier of the Digital Health Portal project that is to hold the shared medical record, the DMP.

Tiers in use. The state news agency AMI, in a report published in 2022, states that patients' health records have been digitised at one health centre, that of Sebkha in Nouakchott-Ouest. The Agenda gives the share of the population holding a shared medical record as 0% in 2021, against a 2025 target of 50%, attributing the figure to the Ministry of Health.

Where data is digitised. At Sebkha in 2022 the Ministry of Health's secretary general said that the whole patient pathway, from consultation to discharge, would be fully digital by 2025.

Last twelve months. The European Commission's 2025 action document counts interoperable digital services, the patient record among them, at 0 in 2024 against a target of 5.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In AMI's 2022 report the secretary general called Sebkha a pilot centre and a model for all the country's health and hospital facilities.

Not held. Nothing held after 2022 shows whether the Sebkha record still runs or has spread to another facility, and where the record is digitised is not stated. No event within the last twelve months is held.

MUS.short: e-Health runs at one regional hospital and several primary structures of its region (May 2026); no count or share of primary clinics is established.
MUS.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. UNDP's case study of February 2025 states that UNDP Mauritius ran the procurement that selected TrioTree Technologies and its consortium for the project it names One Patient, One Record, and that the project has been allocated MUR 600 million, divided into phases. allAfrica reported on 8 January 2026 that Digital Health Company Ltd is a public company under the Ministry of Health and Wellness.

Tiers in use. L'Express reported in May 2026 the health minister saying that the system, which he calls e-Health, is operational at New Flacq Hospital, where testing began on 23 August 2025, and in several primary health care structures of the same region.

Where data is digitised. The system covers the full outpatient cycle from registration to follow-up, with nursing, doctor and pharmacy modules added to phase 1, the minister said. By 30 April 2026 it had recorded more than 126,000 patient registrations, 225,000 visits and 221,000 medical consultations.

Last twelve months. L'Express reported in May 2026 the minister telling Parliament that deployment is scheduled at Jawaharlal Nehru Hospital by September 2026, Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam National Hospital in March 2027 and Dr A.G. Jeetoo and Victoria hospitals no earlier than December 2027.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The primary structures using the system in May 2026 are in the New Flacq region. The ministry's Health Sector Strategic Plan 2020-2024 gave the share of all health facilities using EMR as 0 in 2019, against a target of 100% by 2024.

Not held. The primary structures using the system are neither named nor counted, so no share or count of primary clinics is established. Who pays the MUR 600 million, a current plan naming the system, and whether a record can be retrieved at another facility are not stated.

MWI.short: Mahis is in pilot at one central hospital and selected health centres (September 2026); the number of health centres is not given.
MWI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and Sanitation has rolled out the Malawi Health Care Information System, which it calls Mahis, as reported on 3 September 2026. The Digital Health Governance Framework 2025-2030, signed in June 2025, sets the system's nationwide scale-up across public and private facilities and states that digital health in Malawi continues to rely heavily on donor funding.

Tiers in use. On 3 September 2026 Mahis was in pilot at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital in Blantyre and at selected health centres nationwide.

Where data is digitised. A newspaper's check of the hospital's outpatient department on 3 September 2026 found that registered patients no longer produced health passport books, and first-time patients had their details captured at the registry and were issued a barcode. The ministry says each patient gets a unique identifier held on a server that facilities reach through an interoperability layer. In Zomba District in September 2024, most facilities, particularly rural government clinics, kept no out-patient files, so the paper Health Passport was the only medical record for most people.

Last twelve months. In April 2026 the link between the iCHIS community module for non-communicable diseases and MaHIS at health facilities was being finalised.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Mahis was under pilot at selected health centres nationwide on 3 September 2026. In 2025 the ministry piloted linking the National ID to electronic medical record systems in five health facilities in Karonga District.

Not held. The number of health centres in the pilot is not given, and no hospital beyond Queen Elizabeth Central is named as using the system. Nothing held shows a record retrieved at a second facility, or the community system's link in use.

NAM.short: IHCIMS is fully deployed at two hospitals only, with paper records in most hospitals and clinics (2025 study); primary clinics' use not established.
NAM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and Social Services launched its Integrated Health Care Information Management System (IHCIMS) in Windhoek in 2011, and its own IT department supports the ministry's information systems. Managers interviewed for a study published in March 2026 said the ministry has developed an e-Health Strategy, cited as the National eHealth Strategy 2021-2025, to guide a digital platform for capturing patient data. A study of ministry staff published in September 2025 reports budget constraints as the greatest obstacle and says the ministry is making budgetary provision for IT equipment.

Tiers in use. IHCIMS, launched for every facility, was fully deployed only at Windhoek Central Hospital and Oshakati State Hospital, on the study of September 2025.

Where data is digitised. Practitioners reach a patient's record only through the paper health passport and manual records, and there is no unique patient identifier, the same study states.

Last twelve months. The managers said in the study of March 2026 that the platform was starting with a billing module on pilot at Katutura and Windhoek Central hospitals.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The study of September 2025 states that the ministry still relies on paper records in most hospitals and clinics.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics using an electronic record is held, and no dated event falls in the last twelve months. No funder or budget line for the system is stated, and no strategy running past 2025 is held.

NER.short: Computerised records set up in health centres and district hospitals of three districts (November 2024); no count of centres or place of entry is held.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The mid-term evaluation for Enabel, of November 2024, states that the Enabel project PASS Sutura started the digitalisation with recruited consultancy firms, with the Ministry of Health's digital health directorate involved. PASS Sutura is a Belgian bilateral project with EUR 14.5 million for health over 2022-2026, and a Netherlands co-financing of EUR 3.2 million to 31 March 2025 puts particular emphasis on digitalisation. On 8 July 2026 the health minister opened the workshop validating the costed roadmap of the Schéma Directeur National de la e-Santé 2025-2029.

Tiers in use. By November 2024 the project had set up digitalisation, including computerised medical records and billing, in the integrated health centres (CSI) and district hospitals of Dioundiou, Gothèye and Gaya.

Where data is digitised. Enabel states that a hospital information system built around a computerised medical record was put in place at the district hospitals of Gaya and Gothèye after field missions in February and April 2024.

Last twelve months. At the workshop of 8 July 2026 the Directorate of e-Santé presented OpenClinic, its project for a hospital information system and computerised patient record, as already under way.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The evaluation of November 2024 places the digitalised health centres in the project's three target health districts only. In September 2018 the ministry's strategy reported electronic patient record activity in two health districts, Gaya and Gothèye, of 72.

Not held. No count of health centres using the computerised record is held, and no denominator. Nothing held says whether the record is made at the point of care or keyed afterwards, and no sites or counts are given for OpenClinic.

NGA.short: EMR at the point of care in 100 of Lagos State's 326 primary clinics (May 2025); no national share, and no shared record, is established.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare's Nigeria Digital Health Architecture of December 2025 sets interoperable electronic health record systems across all levels of care as its first pillar. In the memorandum signed with the United States on 19 December 2025, Nigeria commits to roll digital medical records out in 20% of facilities by 2026 and 100% by 2030, and the United States plans approximately US$28 million for an enhanced electronic medical record system over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. The Minister of State for Health told the National Council on Health on 20 November 2025 that over 200 hospitals are integrated with electronic medical records systems. In Lagos State an EMR was in use in primary health care centres in May 2025.

Where data is digitised. In May 2025 the Lagos State Primary Health Care Board described its EMR as working "at the point of care". The federal architecture of December 2025 states that health data systems remain largely siloed and paper based, especially in public facilities.

Last twelve months. On 16 September 2026 the minister of state for health said the electronic medical record systems deployed in health facilities are fragmented and that minimum standards would be set and enforced.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Lagos State Ministry of Health reported on 22 May 2025 the EMR platform deployed in 100 of the state's 326 primary health care facilities.

Not held. No national share or count of primary clinics using an EMR is held; the figure is Lagos State's alone, and the over 200 hospitals have no denominator or tier. No shared record on a unique identifier is evidenced, and Nigeria's own commitment to data systems is not broken down to the EHR.

RWA.short: All 42 district hospitals used an EMR in 2023 and eBuzima reached most public facilities by 2026; a shared record is not established.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Rwanda Biomedical Centre slides of April 2026 present eBuzima as the national system for all public health facilities, served from the Ministry of Health's own domain. In a memorandum signed on 5 December 2025 and running from April 2026 to December 2030, the government commits to expand national EMR systems across all health facilities. The United States plans to allocate US$6,806,292 over 2026 and 2027 to the e-Buzima rollout, and Rwanda commits to pay the ongoing licensing, cloud and hardware costs the United States does not.

Tiers in use. A survey of April and May 2023 found all 42 district hospitals using an electronic medical record system, 35 of them OpenMRS. King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, a referral hospital in Kigali, runs an Integrated Health Management Information System that gives each patient a single record, the Tony Blair Institute reported in July 2026.

Where data is digitised. The April 2026 slides describe eBuzima as centralised, web-based and synchronising records across public facilities.

Last twelve months. By 8 April 2026 eBuzima had been rolled out to the majority of public health facilities, with its HIV key-population and PrEP modules running in one Kigali pilot site.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Tom Frieden wrote in a piece published in September 2026 that eBuzima is in more than two thirds of health centres. The 2023 survey found 71 of 215 randomly sampled public health centres (33.0%) using an electronic medical record system.

Not held. No unique patient identifier and no record retrieved at another facility is established. No count of facilities using eBuzima is held, nor who enters the record at the health centres or where it is keyed.

SDN.short: Hospital management system with electronic medical record launched at two hospital sites on 11 May 2026; routine use and the hospitals' level are not established.
SDN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications launched the hospital management system (HMS) on 11 May 2026 as their own programme, on the Sudan News Agency's report. ICTworks' directory, as of July 2026, lists the Sudan eHealth Strategy of the WHO Global Observatory's 2014 cycle as the operative digital health instrument and states that no replacement has been promulgated.

Tiers in use. Phase one of the HMS started on 11 May 2026 at two hospital sites, Al-Nao hospital in Khartoum state and the diagnostic centre of Gedaref hospital, ahead of gradual expansion to health institutions in other states.

Where data is digitised. An MSc thesis at Sudan University of Science and Technology, of March 2021, states that hospitals in Sudan had no electronic medical records and kept patients' health records on paper.

Last twelve months. A directive published on 30 March 2026 has the Prime Minister ordering hospital systems digitised within two weeks through a first pilot phase at Soba teaching hospital and Gedaref hospital.
