The HMS launched on 11 May 2026 includes an electronic patient record and an electronic medical record.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The first phase directed in March 2026 covers two hospitals only, with wider expansion left to a later phased plan. The thesis of March 2021 states that government clinics had no electronic medical record and depended wholly on paper records.

Not held. Whether the two sites are in routine use, the hospitals' level and where the record is entered are not established. No funding source is named for any system, and no sites or counts are held for SudaHealth, the Khartoum State platform.

SEN.short: The record runs at pilot sites, 1% of 102 health centres (October 2025); health posts are uncounted and retrieval elsewhere is not established.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank, in a paper of January 2026, names the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene as lead agency, deploying the electronic medical record. The ministry's sector policy letter of 25 March 2025 sets the generalisation of the computerised patient record under its Health System Digitalisation Programme 2023-2029. The record is a core activity of the US$46 million health component of the IDA-financed Senegal Digital Economy Acceleration Project.

Tiers in use. The health ministry states that the record, which it calls the Dossier Patient Informatisé, has been in use since November 2024 at the Thierno Birahim Ndao regional hospital in Kaffrine. We Are Tech Africa reported on 30 April 2025 a completed pilot at two hospitals, the Khadim Rassoul health centre and the HLM Fass health post.

Where data is digitised. At the Kaffrine hospital the patient is created in the system at registration and the doctor enters observations directly into it after the consultation, on the ministry's account, since November 2024.

Last twelve months. The World Bank records that a pilot of the record across 51 health centres had not started as of December 2025, delayed by disagreement between the health and digital ministries.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The World Bank's results framework gives 1 per cent of the 102 district-level health centres as using electronic medical records at 31 October 2025. An electronic record was available for 200,000 primary care patients at the same date.

Not held. Retrieval of a patient's record at another facility is not stated, and the 1 per cent counts health centres only, with health posts outside it. Nothing held says whether the 51-centre pilot began in 2026.

SLE.short: EMR runs at Koidu Government Hospital and Wellbody Clinic (2026), Connaught Hospital as a 2023 pilot; the Ministry's national EMR is not shown procured.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. OpenMRS's case study of April 2026 describes the PIH EMR as Partners In Health's own OpenMRS distribution. The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 commits the Government to roll out Electronic Medical Records to all medical facilities by 2030 and names a Ministry of Health directorate as lead. The Ministry's request for expressions of interest of 18 December 2025 states that a donor grant finances the initial phase.

Tiers in use. The case study states that Koidu Government Hospital, a referral centre, uses the PIH EMR and that the EMR has run at Wellbody Clinic since 2015. The Ministry reported on 11 October 2023 that it and Smart Systems Sierra Leone Ltd had launched an EMR pilot at Connaught Hospital in Freetown.

Where data is digitised. The case study states that the EMR at the Maternal Center of Excellence in Koidu is entered at the point of care, with retrospective entry also possible.

Last twelve months. The Maternal Center of Excellence opened on 14 February 2026 with the EMR covering all its inpatient wards. On 18 December 2025 the Ministry's project unit asked firms to express interest in deploying an OpenMRS-based EMR across 300 health facilities.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The case study of April 2026 names one clinic using the PIH EMR, Wellbody Clinic. The Compact of 6 December 2025 gives a baseline of 5 health facilities implementing the system, in a network it puts at about 1,463 public facilities.

Not held. What share of primary clinics keep patient records electronically is not held, nor the present state of the pilots at other primary facilities. The Compact's baseline of 5 facilities is undated, and the Ministry's national EMR is not shown procured.

SOM.short: C+ DDS in over 40 facilities (April 2026) and RAAD in 111 primary facilities (2025). No denominator or unique patient identifier held.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. By its own account the Ministry of Health developed RAAD as a national electronic health record for primary healthcare, implemented between 2023 and 2025. Its bulletin for July to September 2023 says the pilot was supported by the Government of Sweden through SPIDER. The Caafimaad+ Digitalized Data System (C+ DDS) is run by the CaafimaadPlus consortium of ten NGOs, in partnership with the Federal Ministry of Health, and funded by EU Humanitarian Aid, as the consortium stated in April 2026.

Tiers in use. The ministry's case study places RAAD in public primary healthcare facilities only, between 2023 and 2025.

Where data is digitised. RAAD captures clinical data as routine care documentation, in place of an average of 15 paper forms, on the ministry's case study of 2023 to 2025. The consortium said in April 2026 that C+ DDS replaces manual reports with real-time entry and makes a family's record available at any facility on the system.

Last twelve months. The consortium reports growth from a five-facility pilot in mid-2024 to over 40 facilities by April 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In April 2026 the consortium reported C+ DDS operational in over 40 facilities across 9 regions and more than 25 districts of South-Central Somalia. The ministry's case study reports RAAD deployed in 111 public primary healthcare facilities across six states between 2023 and 2025.

Not held. No count of all primary clinics is held to set either figure against, and the two systems' facilities are not shown to be separate. No plan naming an electronic medical record, no unique patient identifier and no tier for the C+ DDS facilities is held.

SSD.short: Only an OpenMRS ART register at five sites, a tracker, is held; no EMR in use or dated statement of paper records sets a rung.
SSD.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record in use is held, and no dated statement that patient records are on paper at every tier. The 22.4% of health facilities that the February 2025 assessment records with facility-wide electronic systems comes with no system named.

STP.short: A patient record was piloted at the central hospital and one health area in 2022; whether it was evaluated or extended is not established.
STP.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Health Development Plan 2023-2032, dated September 2022, sets a strategic axis on expanding what it calls the single clinical process to the whole national health system. The Joint SDG Fund programme's final report of 26 July 2022 states that the Single Process module for patient files was developed inside DHIS2, the Ministry of Health's main information software, and that rolling it out beyond the pilot will be done with funding from other donors.

Tiers in use. In September 2022 the plan placed the record in a pilot phase at the Ayres de Menezes central hospital and the Água Grande Health Area.

Where data is digitised. The report of July 2022 states that patient data is entered from reception through the nurses and doctors, each patient's file reached by a bar code sticker and scanner.

Last twelve months. The plan of September 2022 states that the pilot is to be evaluated before expansion to the whole national health system.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. At 26 July 2022 the Single Process had not been rolled out to other districts and still needed consolidating in the first pilot district, Água Grande. The plan states that computerised clinical records are to be introduced gradually through a pilot model of health centres and the central hospital.

Not held. Nothing is dated after September 2022: whether the pilot was evaluated, consolidated or extended beyond Água Grande is not established. The health area's facilities are not named and no count of facilities using the record is given.

SWZ.short: CMIS in 73% of all health facilities, 233 sites (2026), record shared between clinics; no current plan, domestic budget line or primary-clinic denominator held.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Data.FI described the Client Management Information System (CMIS) in April 2026 as an open-source, government-owned electronic medical record. The Ministry of Health's HMIS unit describes itself as custodian of the digital health systems, with its own in-country developers working on CMIS. Data.FI, a PEPFAR-funded USAID agreement, reported for the period ending March 2024 that it funds and carries out CMIS system development, security assessment and facility network support.

Tiers in use. Data.FI described CMIS in April 2026 as in use in the outpatient department of Piggs Peak Government Hospital and at local health clinics.

Where data is digitised. Data.FI said in April 2026 that clinicians open a client's full record on a unique ID number at their point of service, and that the record is available to clinicians at another clinic if the patient moves district.

Last twelve months. The HMIS unit reported in June 2026 that the integration of CMIS with eLMIS runs for ART medicines only and is ready for a facility-level pilot. In the first quarter of 2026 its developers completed training that produced automated, FHIR-aligned data flows from CMIS to DHIS2.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Data.FI said in April 2026 that CMIS is used in 73% of the country's health facilities, with 233 live sites. For the period ending March 2024 it reported CMIS in use at 75% (247 of 327) of healthcare facilities.

Not held. No current plan naming CMIS and no domestic budget line for it is held. The 73% is a share of all health facilities with no denominator given, and no count of primary clinics alone is held.

SYC.short: A ministry system encompassing electronic medical records, operational since end-2021 (reported January 2024); tiers, point of entry and clinics using it are not established.
SYC.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Seychelles Nation reports the health minister saying on 17 October 2023 that the Ministry of Health is investing in an Electronic Health Information System encompassing Electronic Medical Records, the ministry's name for it. The National Health Strategic Plan 2022-2026 sets specific objective 6.8, "Implement eHIS", and names the Health Care Agency as lead entity, with the Ministry of Health and the Public Health Authority contributing.

Tiers in use. The minister said in October 2023 that the system is to be accessible to all health professionals throughout the health system.

Where data is digitised. At its digital health visioning meeting of 22 January 2024 the ministry said it was trying to link the system with laboratories and X-ray so that doctors get results on their computers.

Last twelve months. A ministry press release carried by Seychelles Nation in January 2024 states that the system has been operational since the end of 2021.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The 2022-2026 plan sets three go-live phases, the first being client registration and appointments across all relevant units.

Not held. The tiers using the system, where the record is entered and the primary clinics using it are not established. Finance is not stated, and nothing dated inside the last twelve months is held.

TCD.short: Visa Medical partnership reported and a ministry meeting on an electronic record (2026); no facility in use, tier or clinic figure held, so no rung.
TCD.summary: Not held. No electronic medical record is held in use at any facility: no tier, no place of digitisation and no clinic figure. What is held is a partnership for Visa Medical reported on 13 August 2026 and a ministry meeting of 15 April 2026 on a Dossier Médical Électronique, with no deployment, pilot site, budget or timetable.

TGO.short: No electronic health record system was established at December 2025, per the World Bank; whether every tier keeps paper records is not established.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's additional-financing paper of 24 December 2025 states that since October 2025 the health ministry has been responsible for the health and insurance systems layer, including the electronic health record (EHR). The financing pays EUR 866,112.50 on establishment of the system and EUR 173,223 for every 10 contracted facilities with an EHR.

Tiers in use. The paper records "No" at December 2025 for the establishment of an electronic health record system.

Where data is digitised. The Togo Digital 2025 strategy of April 2021 plans a digital and centralised medical record, as something to be developed.

Last twelve months. On 24 December 2025 the World Bank put forward additional financing, a EUR 60.6 million credit and US$11 million in grants, with new conditions for establishing an EHR in facilities contracted under the national health insurance scheme, starting with a pilot.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The paper's results framework gives a baseline of 0 facilities contracted with the national health insurance scheme holding an EHR at December 2025, out of about 335 contracted facilities.

Not held. No source states in terms that patient records are on paper at every tier, and the baseline does not cover facilities outside the insurance scheme. Where records are digitised is not held.

TUN.short: Record fully used in 50% of university and 32% of regional hospitals (2025), pilot sites in Nabeul's primary care; no hospital or clinic count.
TUN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. WHO Tunisia stated in April 2024 that the Ministry of Health's Information Technology Centre develops and implements the hospital information management system, with a focus on electronic medical records. The draft National Health Policy of 2019 calls for the generalisation of a single, digitised medical record. The first-line record, which the programme calls the DMI, was developed under Essaha Aziza, a Ministry of Health and European Union programme.

Tiers in use. The World Bank's project document of 2 April 2025 gives the record as fully installed and used in 50 per cent of university hospitals and partially used in the other 50 per cent, and as fully operational in 32 per cent of regional hospitals, partially used in 52 per cent and absent from 16 per cent. In district hospitals it is neither installed nor used.

Where data is digitised. Of primary health care, the same document states that the health system remains largely paper-based and that the DMI pilot faces connectivity and functionality issues.

Last twelve months. The Ministry of Health confirmed on 21 July 2026 that the Sahetna.tn portal, through which citizens are to reach their medical records, had completed technical validation and a cybersecurity audit; it was not yet in service.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Essaha Aziza states that it monitored the DMI's deployment on pilot sites in Nabeul. DH Arab, on the ministry's account at 25 September 2026, has 99 healthcare facilities at various stages of implementing electronic medical records.

Not held. No count of hospitals or of primary clinics using the record is held; the 99 facilities carry no tier and the Nabeul pilot sites no number. The plan is an uncosted draft of 2019, and no domestic budget line for the record is named.

TZA.short: GOT-HoMIS in 23.25% of all health facilities, read as primary clinics (SARA 2023); a shared record is not established.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The mid-term review of the Health Sector Strategic Plan V, published in March 2025, states that the Ministry of Health developed and launched Afya eHMS for all regional hospitals and plans to phase out the vendor-dependent Medipro and E-Medical used in zonal and specialised hospitals. It records that the Digital Health Strategy 2019-2024 had run out and its 2025-2030 successor was still being developed.

Tiers in use. The Citizen reported on 1 September 2026 that electronic medical record coverage had reached 100 percent of national, specialised, zonal and regional referral hospitals, and that adoption had expanded across district hospitals, health centres and dispensaries. The mid-term review of March 2025 states that all 28 regional hospitals use Afya eHMS.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's guidelines of May 2019 state that most confidential health data is held in health facilities in paper-based registers.

Last twelve months. The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health said on 1 October 2025 that the country has an integrated electronic medical records system linking a patient's information from community level through health centres and district hospitals to national level.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The mid-term review, citing the SARA survey of 2023, gives 23.25% of all health facilities using GOT-HoMIS, the government's facility system, against 44.9% of health centres and 10.63% of dispensaries. In March 2025 it states that more than 3,000 primary health care facilities use it as their electronic medical record system.

Not held. Nothing held establishes where the patient record is digitised or whether it can be retrieved at another facility. No financing is stated, no dated event falls in the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging with the EMR.

UGA.short: The ministry's EMR ran in referral and general hospitals, 5 Health Centre IVs and 2 IIIs in 2025; no shared record or clinic share.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's guidelines of 18 September 2024 name the ministry as owner of the Electronic Medical Records System. The US-Uganda memorandum signed on 10 December 2025 names eAfya and ClinicMaster as the Government of Uganda's electronic medical records and sets a functional EMR in all facilities down to Health Centre III by 2028. Under it the United States plans US$113,102,289 for data systems over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. The ministry says that as of 2025 the EMR is in referral and general hospitals and in some health centres. In Kiryandongo district it was in use in September 2026 at the general hospital, Nyakadoti Health Centre III and Mpumwe and Apodorwa Health Centre IIs.

Where data is digitised. The in-charge of Nyakadoti Health Centre III said on 19 September 2026 that patient data must be captured in the EMR at every stage of the visit. A census of all 265 government Health Centre IVs and hospitals, published in October 2025, found 94.3% keeping both paper and digital patient records.

Last twelve months. On 31 March 2026 Makerere University's METS programme handed the UgandaEMR repositories to the Ministry of Health. Health workers told a baraza on 19 September 2026 that the EMR was slowing care in Kiryandongo facilities because of poor connectivity, unstable power and too few computers.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry counts 5 Health Centre IVs and 2 Health Centre IIIs using the EMR as of 2025.

Not held. Nothing held shows a record retrievable at another facility, or what share of primary clinics use the EMR; hospital coverage is disputed between the ministry and a census of government facilities. No domestic budget line for the EMR is held.

ZAF.short: Hospital systems in five provinces and 308 Western Cape primary facilities, August 2025; no national count in use, no shared record established.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Minister of Health told Parliament on 1 August 2025 that the National Department of Health is developing a single common Electronic Medical Record for primary health care facilities. The department's bid document of March 2026 says it developed the EMR itself and that its Digital Health Unit directs implementation.

Tiers in use. The same reply counts Clinicom in 53 Western Cape hospitals, the eHealth system in 42 KwaZulu-Natal public hospitals and HMS2 in 16 Free State hospitals. It states that Mpumalanga, North West, Limpopo and Northern Cape are not implementing such systems at hospitals.

Where data is digitised. The department describes its EMR, in March 2026, as capturing clinical information at the point of care, verified against the patient's identifier in the Health Patient Registration System.

Last twelve months. In March 2026 the department invited bids to scale up its EMR to all fixed primary health care facilities in eight provinces within 18 months. The Free State Department of Health won the Public Sector Digital Innovator Award for deploying its primary health care EMR, SAnews reported in May 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Minister's reply states that the National EMR beta ran in 36 primary health care facilities between 22 October 2024 and 13 February 2025 and that Western Cape's Primary Health Care Information System is implemented in 308. It counts 3,333 primary health care facilities reporting to the 2024/25 Ideal Clinic Assessment.

Not held. No count of primary facilities using the national EMR in 2026 is held, and no total of hospitals against which the provincial counts can be set. Nothing held shows a record retrieved at another facility, and no funding source is named.

ZMB.short: SmartCare Pro was in use at 877 of 3,540 health facilities of all kinds (April 2025); primary clinics' share and shared-record use are not established.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Global Fund's case study of April 2025 states that the Ministry of Health developed SmartCare and describes it as co-financed by the Global Fund. SMART Zambia's national coordinator said on 7 July 2026 that government aims at full national coverage of SmartCare Pro.

Tiers in use. SmartCare 2.0 Hospital Edition went live as a pilot at Ndola Teaching Hospital on 27 April 2026. Interviews of May and June 2019 found some larger health centres and hospitals collecting data in the electronic health record, in select districts.

Where data is digitised. The programme managers' presentation of March 2025 describes SmartCare Pro as capturing the patient encounter at facility level, on a central server that identifies each client uniquely and tracks patients between facilities. The implementers described in January 2026 a nurse at a rural clinic in Kafulafuta identifying a patient by fingerprint to reach his record.

Last twelve months. ITWeb Africa reported on 16 July 2026 that SmartCare Pro and SmartCare 2.0 will be migrated to the government-owned GovLink network, with three Copperbelt hospitals connected first.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Global Fund states that SmartCare Pro is in use at 877 health facilities, against 3,540 health facilities in Zambia, at April 2025. The March 2025 presentation puts SmartCare Legacy and SmartCare Plus together in approximately 1,800 healthcare facilities. SMART Zambia's national coordinator said on 7 July 2026 that SmartCare Pro has been deployed in approximately 80% of health facilities nationwide.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics using SmartCare is held: every figure counts health facilities of all kinds, and the 80% is of deployment, with no numerator or denominator. Use at the primary tier rests on 2019 interviews and one rural clinic, and nothing held shows a record retrieved at a second facility in practice.

ZWE.short: Impilo ran in 1,254 health facilities of all types, of 1,900 planned (August 2025); record retrieval elsewhere and primary clinics' own entry are not established.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Global Fund said in August 2025 that the Government of Zimbabwe has been developing a national EMR system since February 2015, culminating in Impilo, for use in public health facilities. The ministry's National Health Strategy 2021-2025 commits to supporting the deployment of what it calls the electronic health record (Impilo) system. The Global Fund has put over US$43.1 million into digital health in Zimbabwe since 2014, US$9.85 million of it in the 2024-2026 grant cycle.

Tiers in use. The Permanent Secretary for Health and Child Care told The Sunday Mail on 17 November 2024 that the facilities with Impilo are spread across provinces and districts and include clinics, hospitals and other health centres.

Where data is digitised. A 2025 abstract on the DHIS2 community site states that Impilo captures real-time clinical and administrative data for services including HIV testing, antiretroviral therapy and maternal and child health, stored in centralised repositories and a national data warehouse.

Last twelve months. The Herald on 23 September 2026 described Impilo as the Ministry of Health's own electronic health records platform.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Global Fund reports 1,254 health facilities implementing Impilo as of August 2025, with deployment planned for all 1,900 health facilities. The Permanent Secretary put deployment at 1,178 health facilities on 17 November 2024. The Matabeleland South provincial health team reported 110 of the province's 153 health facilities (71.9%) with Impilo fully functional in May 2025.

Not held. Nothing held says an Impilo record can be retrieved at another facility. The counts are of facilities of every type where Impilo is deployed, not of primary clinics entering records, and no strategy current at 30 September 2026 is held.
